title: Profile target_function smart-skip caching under AdamW
description:
The 'smart skip' logic in target_function_wrapper (python/helpers/helper_minimizer.py L62-L89) maintains previous_guess[0] = last-call x, and target_function only re-runs zcat.update() for categories whose indices changed between successive calls. This is well-suited to coordinate descent or L-BFGS-B (which probes one coordinate at a time during finite-difference Jacobian estimation), but the AdamW path in python/utilities/adamw_minimizer.py computes a central-difference gradient by alternating fun(x_fwd) and fun(x_bwd) for every coordinate i in sequence. Because x_fwd and x_bwd each differ from the previous call in (typically) only one index but x_fwd[i] != x_bwd[i-1] in general, the set of 'changed' indices may be larger than necessary and the cache hit rate is probably much lower than under L-BFGS-B. Worth measuring before deciding whether to (a) drop the wrapper, (b) extend it with a small key->result LRU keyed on (lead_idx, sublead_idx, x[lead], x[sublead], x[smear_lead], x[smear_sub]), or (c) push caching into zcat.update itself.

## Context
See conversation 2026-05-23 review for full context. Cross-ref: python/utilities/adamw_minimizer.py finite-difference loop and python/helpers/helper_minimizer.py target_function.
acceptance_criteria: Profile a representative step4 minimization with AdamW. Report: (1) total fun() calls, (2) total zcat.update() calls, (3) fraction of zcat.update() calls that would have been skipped if results were cached on the per-cat parameter tuple, (4) wall-clock breakdown for numba histogram vs. EMD vs. python overhead. Decide on (a/b/c) above based on numbers and either implement or document why no change is needed.
